slides: Welcome back. Before the harder absolute-value questions, I want to give you two tools. You'll meet them again and again in the next questions.

slides.say: First, a square and the bars do the same thing to the sign. They both remove it. So the absolute value of x, squared, is just x squared.
at: So the absolute value of x

slides.say: Let's see it in numbers. Take negative six. Bars first, the absolute value of negative six is six, and six squared is thirty-six. Without the bars, negative six squared is also thirty-six.
Why does this work? Squaring kills the sign, and so do the bars. So once you square, it doesn't matter if the bars are there or not.
And you saw the other direction with roots. The square root of x squared is the absolute value of x, not x. The root of negative six squared is the root of thirty-six, and that's six.
at: The square root of x squared

slides.say: [short pause] Second, the order inside the bars doesn't matter. a minus b and b minus a are always opposites. Opposites attract, so together they cancel out to zero. But each one alone is the same distance from zero.
Two minus nine is negative seven, and its absolute value is seven. Nine minus two is seven. The same.
So inside the bars, I can switch the order. a minus b, or b minus a, it's the same thing.

[short pause] Now the distance. Remember from the lesson, the absolute value of x minus a number is the distance between x and that number. Nine minus two in bars is seven, and from two to nine is exactly seven steps.
at: the absolute value of x minus a number

slides.say: So how do I read the absolute value of x minus three, smaller than four? x is less than four steps away from three.
Start at three. Four steps to the left is negative one, and four steps to the right is seven. So x is anywhere between negative one and seven, not including them.
And careful with a plus inside. x plus five is x minus negative five, so it's the distance from negative five.
So two tools. Squares and bars both remove the sign, and the order inside the bars doesn't matter. And bars around x minus a number mean distance. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next video.
